note: Automated candidate collection. Not reviewed under this publication's evidence standard. Promote entries to the reviewed radar only through the website's curation process.

items.quantitative_outcome: Dataset announced, not a measured operating outcome: “100 million” single-cell RNA-seq profiles, “more than 11,000” proteomic secretome profiles, and responses to “over 150,000” perturbation conditions. Measured against: none stated. Reported by: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio in their announcement, carried by BioSpace.
items.signal: The partners plan to create Cascade, a large multimodal immune-biology dataset, with foundational commitments from GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, Graph Therapeutics, and Turbine. This is a distinctive data-access move that could support AI models; no demonstrated operating benefit is reported.

items.quantitative_outcome: “a 3X improvement in survival” for a patient subgroup identified through analysis of a failed Phase III pancreatic cancer trial. Measured against: the broader trial population or another comparator was not specified in the available report. Reported by: Bullfrog AI CEO Singh at the LD Micro conference, as relayed in an Investing.com conference report.
items.signal: Bullfrog AI said its analysis of Eleison Pharmaceuticals’ trial data identified a subgroup and biomarkers associated with improved survival. The report provides a numerical claim, but does not state the comparison details or establish that the analysis prospectively improved trial outcomes.

items.quantitative_outcome: No operating outcome stated. The announced move makes Hamilton Lane's institutional-grade private-markets data—covering more than 70,000 funds and 240,000 assets, plus proprietary fund- and deal-level benchmarks—available within FactSet's portfolio analytics platform.
items.signal: Distinctive data-access partnership: Hamilton Lane is embedding its private-markets dataset and proprietary benchmarks in FactSet's analytics platform. This could give users an uncommon data resource for integrated public/private portfolio analysis; the announcement does not report measured benefits.

items.quantitative_outcome: The source reports that the AI underwriting copilot “reduced the time underwriters spend processing complex life insurance cases by 59%.”
items.signal: Reported processing-time reduction for complex life-insurance underwriting. The report describes internal measurements; it does not state a comparison group or a before-and-after baseline, and the result has not been independently validated.

items.quantitative_outcome: The source reports a “20% efficiency improvement in that area this year” for deep credit analysis.
items.signal: A quantified efficiency gain in deep credit analysis, but the report does not specify the measurement method, baseline, or comparator, nor clearly attribute the result to a particular AI tool.
items.source: Insurewire, AI at insurers deployment database (page 5)

items.comparator: Anthropic’s earlier Mythos 5.1 result and Opus 5.5 tested without safeguards; the source describes an October evaluation of 1,829 published vulnerabilities.
items.quantitative_outcome: The source reports: “Mythos 5.2 achieved an 89.6 percent success rate, compared with 78.3 percent for Mythos 5.1 and 81.3 percent for Opus 5.5 when tested without safeguards.” This is a known-vulnerability rediscovery evaluation, not a measured zero-day detection rate.
items.signal: Reported improvement on an internal vulnerability rediscovery evaluation, a weak signal of improved vulnerability-discovery capability. The result is vendor-reported and the source cautions that evaluation design affects results.
items.source: Acid Peak, reporting Anthropic’s model launch and evaluation results

items.comparator: No explicit comparator stated in the available report; live commercial traffic is the operating context.
items.quantitative_outcome: “improvements of up to approximately 20% in spectral efficiency under live commercial traffic”
items.signal: A live-network AI-RAN trial at London’s Paddington Giga Site used predictive AI to optimise radio resources. The reported spectral-efficiency gain is a measured operating benefit, but the source does not specify a control period or matched baseline.
items.source: Tecknexus, AI & Automation Insights October 2026: AI-RAN Goes Live

items.comparator: Initial lab measurements; no non-AI baseline or comparison method stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “initial lab measurements of AI-based uplink channel estimation demonstrated typical throughput improvements of 10% to 15%, with gains increasing as radio channel complexity increased.”
items.signal: AI-based channel estimation was validated alongside commercial 5G RAN software in lab tests. The reported result is a measured throughput gain, but it remains a lab result, with field validation planned.
items.source: TelecomTV, Nvidia boasts greater AI-RAN and AI factory traction with telcos; the article quotes Deutsche Telekom’s announcement.

items.comparator: No comparator stated; the benefit is an estimate based on preliminary data, not a reported before-and-after result.
items.quantitative_outcome: Honeywell estimates AI-enabled optimization “could deliver operational benefit of more than 29 cents a barrel” and “more than $60 million in gross benefit per year” at full-capacity throughput.
items.signal: Forge Plant Cognition is launching at Dangote’s Lekki refinery. Honeywell describes a facility-specific estimate based on preliminary data; it excludes implementation costs and is not a measured realized outcome. The release identifies refinery data and operating context, but does not establish a distinctive or exclusive dataset.
